soundness_flags.label: ass:vanishing-modulus
soundness_flags.one_line: The combined condition e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+delta_T→0 is a proposal-specific attraction envelope, not Mourrat's standard martingale-CLT condition; retag it novel and justify its uniform use.

soundness_flags.label: ass:basin-nondegeneracy
soundness_flags.one_line: Uniform two-sided covariance bounds for every named basin are stronger than Saco's variance-growth condition and are not supported by the cited pointwise theorem; retag this as a novel class condition.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 1
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed matrices and c alone neither specify Sigma nor construct a law/recursion in the finite-attractor class, so they do not establish that Theorems 3 and 4 can simultaneously be instantiated as claimed.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorems 1–2 / ass:finite-tail-selection through ass:uniform-attraction-modulus
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Finite tail selection, positive basin mass, and the Cesaro attraction modulus are assumed class-membership conditions; the exact Guo--Xu recursion is not asserted to satisfy them.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Field-tier conditional result: uniform stable-mixture and realized-QV inference holds for laws in the common-envelope finite-attractor class, while membership and the separatrix rate for the exact Guo--Xu recursion remain open.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, lines 251–264 and 291–312; Section 3.1, lines 337–346
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines scaled inverse-propensity convergence, proves a deterministic Gaussian IPW-Z limit under it, and presents the clipped-LinUCB pathology as a concrete numerical example with Gaussian noise.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorem 5.14 and proof, lines 442–475; Design A, lines 508–518
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 5.14 proves pointwise fixed-horizon realized-QV studentized normality without deterministic variance stabilization; Design A has a two-regime random long-run variance. Its variance-growth condition is only a lower growth condition, not uniform basinwise matrix control.
Directional stability is a target-specific deterministic stabilization condition, weaker than full-matrix stability, used to obtain normal and efficient adaptive inference.
The article gives a lower bound on convergence to a prescribed point in its domain of attraction for recursions with finitely many possible limit points.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author-hosted PDF corresponding to Bernoulli 19(2), 2013, pp. 633–645
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and Introduction, PDF page 1 lines 3–21 and 52–68
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies quantitative Gaussian approximation from normalized quadratic-variation convergence plus a Lindeberg condition; it does not state the proposal's combined e_T attraction modulus.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Retag the attraction envelope and basinwise covariance bounds as novel conditions, state why common constants are empirically defensible across a deployment family, and distinguish them from Saco's pointwise variance-growth hypothesis.
Repair Proposition 1 by specifying Sigma and giving an explicit bounded two-arm finite-attractor law with the stated V_1,V_2, positive basin masses, and the required score/Jacobian properties.

Turn the Guo--Xu separatrix handle into a quantitative membership theorem for a bounded-noise analogue, including a proved rho_T rate and a near-boundary obstruction; that would connect the conditional class to a concrete adaptive algorithm.

recommended_next_step: Revise the two mislabeled standard assumptions and make the directional/matrix separation an actual in-class construction; then retain the conditional field-tier finite-attractor frontier for Stage 0.
